                           FINAL BRIEF OF JOHN B. BRADLEY III

BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS

I. INTRODUCTION

COMES NOW John B. Bradley aka John B. Bradley III ("pro se Intervenor"), of the Lazy S
Ranch Party 433 appearing pro se, and respectfully ﬁles this Final Brief in opposition to the
Joint Application of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services
Corporation.

The issue before the Commission is not whether additional transmission may someday
beneﬁt Texas. The issue is whether the Applicants proved, by a preponderance of the
evidence, that this Application satisﬁes the requirements of PURA § 37.056, including all
factors contained in PURA § 37.056(c), and Commission Rule 16 Texas Administrative Code
§ 25.101(b)(3)(B).

The evidence demonstrates they did not.

II. PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT
                                                               FINAL BRIEF OF JOHN B. BRADLEY
                                                                         PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
                                                                SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
                                                                                   Page 1 of 5
 1. The Applicants relied primarily upon ERCOT planning assumptions, the Permian
   Basin Reliability Plan, and House Bill 5066 to establish project need.

2. The Applicants did not establish that additional local generation, generation nearer
   projected load, or other less burdensome alternatives could not satisfy projected
   future demand.

3. The Applicants presented no project-speciﬁc evidence demonstrating that this
   transmission line will lower electric costs for Texas consumers or provide
   measurable economic beneﬁts commensurate with its cost.

4. The Application asks Texas ratepayers to ﬁnance one of the largest transmission
   projects in Texas history while o ering largely generalized regional beneﬁts.

5. The Applicants relied upon generalized regional planning objectives rather than
   project-speciﬁc evidence demonstrating that routing through the Lazy S Ranch
   represents the most reasonable balance of all statutory considerations.

6. The evidence established permanent impacts to the Lazy S Ranch, including
   impacts to community values, continuous family stewardship, agricultural
   operations, historical resources, aesthetic values, wildlife habitat, environmental
   integrity, artesian water resources, and future residential use.

7. The evidence established that uncertainty remains regarding environmental
   resources, archaeological resources, cultural resources, ﬂoodplain impacts, and
   other route-speciﬁc conditions.

8. Signiﬁcant environmental and cultural resource evaluations remain incomplete and
   will occur after any approval of the Application.

9. The Applicants did not establish that the beneﬁts of the proposed routing outweigh
   the permanent burdens imposed upon the Lazy S Ranch or similarly situated
   landowners.

10. The Applicants did not establish that the proposed routing reasonably minimizes
    adverse impacts or maximizes the use of compatible existing corridors where
    practicable.

11. The evidentiary record demonstrates that important statutory factors remain
    uncertain while the impacts to a ected landowners are immediate, direct, and
    permanent.

                                                           FINAL BRIEF OF JOHN B. BRADLEY
                                                                     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
                                                            SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
                                                                              Page 2 of 5
 III. CONCLUSIONS OF LAW

   1. The Applicants bear the burden of proving, by a preponderance of the evidence, that
      the requested Certiﬁcate of Convenience and Necessity satisﬁes the requirements
      of PURA and applicable Commission rules.

   2. PURA § 37.056 requires the Commission to consider all applicable statutory factors,
      including adequacy of existing service, need for additional service, community
      values, recreational and park areas, historical and aesthetic values, environmental
      integrity, and the probable improvement of service or lowering of cost to consumers.

   3. The evidence does not establish, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the
      Application satisﬁes the requirements of PURA § 37.056.

   4. The Applicants failed to establish that the proposed routing appropriately balances
      the statutory factors contained in PURA § 37.056(c), including community values,
      historical and aesthetic values, environmental integrity, and the probable
      improvement of service or lowering of cost to consumers.

   5. The Applicants failed to establish that the proposed routing complies with 16 Texas
      Administrative Code § 25.101(b)(3)(B), because the record does not demonstrate
      that adverse impacts have been reasonably minimized or that compatible existing
      rights-of-way and corridors have been utilized where practicable.

   6. Because the Applicants failed to satisfy their burden of proof, the requested
      Certiﬁcate of Convenience and Necessity should be denied.



IV. CONCLUSION

The Applicants ask the Commission to approve an unprecedented transmission project
based largely upon projections of future need while imposing substantial costs upon Texas
ratepayers and permanent burdens upon private landowners.

The record demonstrates signiﬁcant uncertainty regarding project-speciﬁc need,
environmental review, cultural resources, consumer beneﬁt, and routing impacts.

Conversely, the impacts to the Lazy S Ranch are certain, substantial, and permanent.



                                                             FINAL BRIEF OF JOHN B. BRADLEY
                                                                       PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
                                                              SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
                                                                                Page 3 of 5
 Texas law places the burden upon the Applicants to prove that this Application satisﬁes
every requirement of PURA § 37.056 and Commission Rule § 25.101.

They failed to meet that burden.



V. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Pro Se Intervenor John B. Bradley III respectfully
requests that the Administrative Law Judges recommend that the Public Utility
Commission deny the Joint Application because the Applicants failed to establish, by a
preponderance of the evidence, that the Application satisﬁes the requirements of PURA §
37.056, including the statutory factors contained in PURA § 37.056(c), and 16 Texas
Administrative Code § 25.101(b)(3)(B).

In the alternative, should the Commission determine that a certiﬁcate should issue,
Intervenor respectfully requests that the Commission reject any routes with Segments E8,
E9, F21, F22, and G71, avoid the Lazy S Ranch, and grant such further relief to which
Intervenor may be justly entitled.

Respectfully submitted,



John B. Bradley III
Party 433
Pro Se Intervenor
Lazy S Ranch
